title: Understanding GitHub Actions Runners knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Understanding GitHub Actions Runners?
options: A runner is the execution environment that receives a scheduled job, runs its steps, and reports results; filesystem state is not automatically shared across separate jobs.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: A runner is the execution environment that receives a scheduled job, runs its steps, and reports results; filesystem state is not automatically shared across separate jobs.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of understanding github actions runners: A runner is the execution environment that receives a scheduled job, runs its steps, and reports results; filesystem state is not automatically shared across separate jobs. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.
